verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 14 & 15: Validity and Renewal of Driving Licences
1. Learner's Licence (LL):
- Valid throughout India for a period of six months from the date of issue.
- Mandatory waiting period to apply for permanent licence: 30 days after learner's licence issuance.

officialTitle: Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (CMVR - Rules & Compliance)
section: Section 14 & 15: Validity and Renewal of Driving Licences
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
2. Non-Transport Driving Licence (Private Cars and Two-Wheelers):
- Issued to individuals below 30 years of age: Valid until the holder attains 40 years of age.
- Issued to individuals aged between 30 and 50 years: Valid for 10 years.
- Issued to individuals aged between 50 and 55 years: Valid until the holder attains 60 years of age.
- Issued to individuals aged above 55 years: Valid for 5 years.

- For transport vehicles carrying dangerous or hazardous goods: Valid for three years, subject to completion of mandatory refresher training course.

- Application for renewal can be filed from one year prior to expiry up to one year after expiry.
- If the application for renewal is made within one year after expiry, the licence is renewed without re-testing.
- If the application for renewal is made more than one year after expiry, the applicant must undergo and pass the formal driving competence test again under Section 15(1).

verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 6: Display of Badges by Public Service Vehicle Drivers
Every driver of a public service vehicle, stage carriage bus, or contract carriage auto-rickshaw in Delhi shall display an authorized metal or digital badge issued by the licensing authority, engraved with the driver's registered serial number and photograph.

officialTitle: Delhi Motor Vehicles Rules 1993
section: Rule 11: Auto-Rickshaw Fare Meters and Passenger Carriage
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 11: Auto-Rickshaw Fare Meters and Passenger Carriage
Every auto-rickshaw and motor cab operating within the National Capital Territory of Delhi shall be fitted with a tamper-proof electronic fare meter calibrated according to the rates notified by the Government of NCT of Delhi. Refusal to ply or demanding fares in excess of the digital meter reading constitutes a violation punishable under Section 178 of the Act.

officialTitle: Delhi Motor Vehicles Rules 1993
section: Rule 53: Clean Fuel (CNG/EV) Mandate for Public Transport in Delhi
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 53: Clean Fuel (CNG/EV) Mandate for Public Transport in Delhi
All commercial passenger transport vehicles, including city buses, taxis, and auto-rickshaws registered in Delhi, shall operate exclusively on clean alternative fuels such as Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) or battery electric propulsion. Entry of non-compliant commercial diesel vehicles into notified low-emission zones is strictly prohibited.

officialTitle: Delhi Motor Vehicles Taxation Act 1962
section: Section 3: Levy of road tax on motor vehicles
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 3: Levy of road tax on motor vehicles
Subject to the other provisions of this Act, there shall be levied and collected on all motor vehicles used or kept for use in Delhi a tax at the rates specified in the First Schedule to this Act. One-time road tax is payable at the time of initial vehicle registration based on vehicle invoice price, fuel type, and engine displacement.

officialTitle: Delhi Motor Vehicles Taxation Act 1962
section: Section 3A: Environment Compensation Charge and Green Cess
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 3A: Environment Compensation Charge and Green Cess
In addition to the road tax levied under Section 3, an Environment Compensation Charge or Green Tax shall be levied on transport and commercial diesel vehicles entering or operating within the National Capital Territory of Delhi to mitigate air pollution and support sustainable public transport initiatives.

officialTitle: Delhi Motor Vehicles Taxation Act 1962
section: Section 13: Penalties for non-payment of road tax
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 13: Penalties for non-payment of road tax
Whoever fails to pay the motor vehicle road tax within the statutory grace period of thirty days shall be liable to pay a penalty at the rate of two per cent per month on the overdue tax amount, and the vehicle is liable to be impounded by the transport department or enforcement wing until full tax and penalty clearance is produced.

officialTitle: Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules 1989
section: Rule 22: High-Tech Automated E-Challan Enforcement and Traffic Management
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 22: High-Tech Automated E-Challan Enforcement and Traffic Management
In the State of Karnataka, traffic enforcement authorities in Bengaluru and other urban centers are authorized to deploy automated contactless enforcement systems, including Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras, red light violation detection (RLVD) systems, and contactless radar guns for capturing traffic offences under Chapter XIII of the Act.

officialTitle: Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules 1989
section: Rule 126: Taxi and Maxi-Cab Fare Meters and Digital Billing
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 126: Taxi and Maxi-Cab Fare Meters and Digital Billing
Every motor cab operating under city permits in Karnataka shall be equipped with a digital fare meter integrated with thermal receipt printers or digital GPS-based fare calculation systems compliant with State Transport Authority regulations. Overcharging or refusing carriage to passengers without lawful cause constitutes an offence under the KMVR rules.

officialTitle: Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules 1989
section: Rule 130: Safety Equipment for Two-Wheeled Motor Vehicles
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 130: Safety Equipment for Two-Wheeled Motor Vehicles
Both the rider and pillion passenger on a two-wheeled motorcycle in Karnataka shall wear protective headgear (helmets) conforming to Indian Standards specifications (IS 4151). Failure to wear a helmet is subject to compounding under Section 194D with a fine of Rs. 1,000 and three months driving licence suspension.

GOVERNMENT OF MAHARASHTRA

State Statutory Rules governing regional transport authorities, stage carriages, school buses, and road regulations across Maharashtra

officialTitle: Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Rules 1989
section: Rule 24: Special Safety Regulations for School Buses in Maharashtra
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 24: Special Safety Regulations for School Buses in Maharashtra
Every motor vehicle used for the carriage of school children in Maharashtra shall be painted in highway golden yellow colour with the words 'School Bus' prominently written on the front and rear. The bus shall be fitted with horizontal window grills, emergency exit doors with alarm buzzers, speed governors calibrated to 40 km/h, GPS location trackers, and CCTV cameras. A trained female attendant shall be present on all trips carrying female pupils.

officialTitle: Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Rules 1989
section: Rule 112: Carriage of Goods on Motor Vehicles
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 112: Carriage of Goods on Motor Vehicles
No motor vehicle shall carry goods exceeding the permissible laden weight recorded in the certificate of registration or projecting horizontally more than thirty centimetres beyond the outer edge of the tyres. Overhang beyond the rear body must display a red flag by day and a red light by night.

officialTitle: Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Rules 1989
section: Rule 115: Noise and Decibel Limits for Vehicle Horns in Urban Areas
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 115: Noise and Decibel Limits for Vehicle Horns in Urban Areas
No motor vehicle in urban areas of Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur, and other municipal corporations in Maharashtra shall be fitted with multi-toned, musical, or air pressure horns. Use of horns within declared Silence Zones (surrounding hospitals, educational institutions, and courts) is prohibited and subject to immediate compoundable fines.

officialTitle: Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Taxation Act
section: Section 3: Levy of tax on motor vehicles in Maharashtra
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 3: Levy of tax on motor vehicles in Maharashtra
A tax shall be leviable on all motor vehicles used or kept for use in the State of Maharashtra at the rates specified in the First Schedule. For non-transport passenger vehicles (cars and two-wheelers), one-time tax (OTT) is assessed on the registration cost, with concessional slabs for battery-operated electric vehicles (EVs).

officialTitle: Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Taxation Act
section: Section 9: Refund of tax on vehicle removal or deregistration
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 9: Refund of tax on vehicle removal or deregistration
Where a motor vehicle in respect of which tax has been paid is removed to any other State or Union Territory on permanent transfer, or where the registration of the vehicle is cancelled due to destruction or scrap, the registered owner shall be entitled to a pro-rata refund of the one-time tax for the unexpired statutory period.

officialTitle: Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Taxation Act
section: Section 16: Recovery of arrears of tax and penalty
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 16: Recovery of arrears of tax and penalty
Any tax or penalty due under this Act may be recovered in the same manner as an arrear of land revenue. Transport enforcement officers are authorized to seize and detain vehicles operating without tax payment until the arrears together with statutory simple interest are fully discharged.

Rule 3: Application for All India Tourist Authorization and Permit
An application for grant of an All India Tourist Permit for a tourist vehicle shall be made electronically on the Parivahan portal to the designated State Transport Authority accompanied by the prescribed composite fee depending on seating capacity.

documentTitle: Morth All India Tourist Vehicles Rules 2023
officialTitle: Morth All India Tourist Vehicles Rules 2023

verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 4: Scope and Validity of Permit
An All India Tourist Permit shall be valid throughout the territory of India without the requirement of obtaining separate individual state permits or paying local road taxes at state border checkposts. The permit shall be granted for a period of thirty days or one year or three years or five years at a time.

documentTitle: Morth All India Tourist Vehicles Rules 2023
officialTitle: Morth All India Tourist Vehicles Rules 2023
section: Rule 7: Conditions of Tourist Vehicle Operation
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 7: Conditions of Tourist Vehicle Operation
Every tourist vehicle operating under an All India Tourist Permit shall display the words 'All India Tourist Vehicle' on the front and rear of the vehicle in bold letters. The vehicle shall be equipped with a functional vehicle location tracking device (VLTD) and an emergency panic button compliant with AIS-140 standards.

documentTitle: Morth All India Tourist Vehicles Rules 2023
officialTitle: Morth All India Tourist Vehicles Rules 2023
section: Section 192A: Penalty for using vehicle without permit
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 192A: Penalty for using vehicle without permit
Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be used in contravention of the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 66 or in contravention of any condition of a permit shall be punishable for the first offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with a fine of ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000), or with both.

Rule 139: Production of licence and certificate of registration
The driver or a person in charge of a motor vehicle shall produce the certificate of registration, insurance, fitness and permit, the driving licence and any other relevant documents on demand by any police officer in uniform or any other officer authorized by the State Government in this behalf.
Provided that if any or all of the documents are not in his possession at the time of demand, the person shall either produce them in electronic form through the DigiLocker platform or the mParivahan mobile application, which shall be accepted as valid proof of the documents under the Information Technology Act, 2000 (21 of 2000) and the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.

verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority

Rule 139A: Time limit for production of documents
If the documents are not produced immediately in electronic or physical form at the time of inspection, the driver or owner of the motor vehicle shall produce the certificate of registration, insurance, fitness, permit, and driving licence in physical or electronic form within seven (7) days from the date of demand before the police officer or the authorized transport official at the concerned police station or office of the licensing authority.

documentTitle: Morth Digilocker Mparivahan Digital Documents Rule 139
officialTitle: Morth Digilocker Mparivahan Digital Documents Rule 139

verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 4 of the Information Technology Act, 2000: Legal recognition of electronic records
Where any law provides that information or any other matter shall be in writing or in the typewritten or printed form, then, notwithstanding anything contained in such law, such requirement shall be deemed to have been satisfied if such information or matter is rendered or made available in an electronic form and accessible so as to be usable for a subsequent reference. Physical seizure of documents is strictly prohibited when valid electronic documents are made available on DigiLocker or mParivahan.

Rule 4: Service of Notice and Grievance Redressal Mechanism
(1) Notice of the e-challan must be transmitted to the registered owner's mobile number via SMS and email within fifteen (15) days of detection.
(2) If the vehicle was sold, stolen, or driven by another person, the registered owner may file an online representation or contest the challan within fifteen (15) days through the Parivahan portal (echallan.parivahan.gov.in).

text:
Section 134A: Protection of Good Samaritans
(1) A Good Samaritan shall not be liable for any civil or criminal action for any injury to or death of an accident victim caused due to their negligence in providing emergency medical or non-medical care or assistance.
(2) The Central Government may make rules regarding the examination and interrogation of a Good Samaritan, protecting them from discrimination, coercion, or harassment by police authorities or hospitals.

documentTitle: Morth Protection Of Good Samaritans Rules
officialTitle: Morth Protection Of Good Samaritans Rules

verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 3: Rights and Protections of a Good Samaritan at Hospitals
(1) Any person who takes an injured road accident victim to a hospital or medical clinic shall be allowed to leave immediately after providing the victim's location or details if known, without answering unnecessary questions.
(2) No hospital, doctor, or medical establishment shall compel a Good Samaritan to provide their personal name, address, telephone number, relationship to the victim, or proof of identity.
(3) No hospital shall demand any registration fees or upfront monetary deposit from a Good Samaritan as a condition for initiating immediate medical treatment or emergency resuscitation of an injured person.
(4) Denial of immediate trauma or emergency medical treatment to an injured accident victim is a severe violation punishable under law.

documentTitle: Morth Protection Of Good Samaritans Rules
officialTitle: Morth Protection Of Good Samaritans Rules
section: Rule 4: Police Interrogation and Witness Procedures
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 4: Police Interrogation and Witness Procedures
(1) A Good Samaritan shall not be compelled to become a witness in any legal or criminal proceedings arising out of the accident.
(2) Where a Good Samaritan chooses voluntarily to give evidence as a witness, the examination by police authorities:
(a) Shall be conducted at a time and place of the Good Samaritan's convenience, such as their residence or place of business;
(b) The police officer conducting the examination shall not wear police uniform and shall conduct the inquiry in a civil and courteous manner;
(c) The statement may be recorded through video conferencing or digital electronic means if requested by the Good Samaritan.
(3) Under no circumstances shall a Good Samaritan be detained or kept overnight at any police station.

documentTitle: Morth Protection Of Good Samaritans Rules

section: Rule 5: Cash Rewards and Recognition Scheme for Good Samaritans
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 5: Cash Rewards and Recognition Scheme for Good Samaritans
(1) Under the MoRTH Good Samaritan Scheme (Notification No. RT-25035/101/2017-RS), any individual who saves the life of an accident victim by rushing them to a hospital within the Golden Hour (the first hour following trauma injury) shall be eligible for:
(a) A cash award of five thousand rupees (Rs. 5,000) per incident;
(b) A Certificate of Appreciation issued by the District Appraisal Committee.
(2) An individual may be recognized multiple times for distinct life-saving rescue acts. National annual awards of one lakh rupees (Rs. 1,00,000) are conferred upon the top ten Good Samaritans nationally.

(1) Every transport vehicle, other than three-wheelers, quadricycles, and two-wheelers, manufactured on or after the 1st day of October, 2015, shall be equipped or fitted by the vehicle manufacturer with a speed limiting device (speed governor) having maximum pre-set speed conforming to the standard AIS:018/2001, as amended from time to time.

text:
Section 3: Necessity for driving licence
No person shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place unless he holds an effective driving licence issued to him authorizing him to drive the vehicle; and no person shall so drive a transport vehicle other than a motor cab or motor cycle hired for his own use or rented under any scheme unless his driving licence specifically entitles him so to do.

officialTitle: Motor Vehicles Act 1988 Principal
section: Section 39: Necessity for registration
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 39: Necessity for registration
No person shall drive any motor vehicle and no owner of a motor vehicle shall cause or permit the vehicle to be driven in any public place or in any other place unless the vehicle is registered in accordance with this Chapter and the certificate of registration of the vehicle has not been suspended or cancelled and the vehicle carries a registration mark displayed in the prescribed manner.

officialTitle: Motor Vehicles Act 1988 Principal
section: Section 146: Necessity for insurance against third party risk
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 146: Necessity for insurance against third party risk
No person shall use, except as a passenger, or cause or allow any other person to use, a motor vehicle in a public place, unless there is in force in relation to the use of the vehicle by that person or that other person, as the case may be, a policy of insurance complying with the requirements of this Chapter.

Section 177: General provision for punishment of offences
Whoever contravenes any provision of this Act or of any rule, regulation or notification made thereunder shall, if no penalty is provided for the offence under this Act, be punishable:
(a) For the first offence, with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees (Rs. 500);
(b) For any second or subsequent offence, with fine which may extend to one thousand five hundred rupees (Rs. 1,500).

verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority

Section 177A: Penalty for contravention of regulations made under Section 118
Whoever contravenes the regulations such as lane driving regulations, violation of traffic signals, or rules of the road regulations made under Section 118 shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than five hundred rupees (Rs. 500) but which may extend to one thousand rupees (Rs. 1,000).

Section 178: Penalty for travelling without pass or ticket and for dereliction of duty on the part of conductor and refusal to ply contract carriage
(1) Whoever travels in a stage carriage without having a proper pass or ticket with him or not being produced shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees (Rs. 500).
(3) If the holder of a permit or driver of a contract carriage refuses to ply the contract carriage or carry the agreed passengers, they shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees (Rs. 500).

verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 179: Disobedience of orders, obstruction and refusal of information
(1) Whoever wilfully disobeys any direction lawfully given by any person or authority empowered under this Act, or obstructs any person or authority in the discharge of their functions, shall be punishable with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees (Rs. 2,000).
(2) Whoever, being required by or under this Act to supply any information, withholds such information or gives information which he knows to be false, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees (Rs. 2,000), or with both.

section: Section 180: Allowing unauthorized persons to drive vehicles
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 180: Allowing unauthorized persons to drive vehicles
Whoever, being the owner or person in charge of a motor vehicle, causes or permits any other person who does not satisfy the provisions of Section 3 or Section 4 to drive the vehicle, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine of five thousand rupees (Rs. 5,000), or with both.

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)

verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority

Section 181: Driving vehicles in contravention of Section 3 or Section 4 (Driving without a valid Driving Licence or underage driving)
Whoever drives a motor vehicle in contravention of Section 3 (necessity for driving licence) or Section 4 (age limit in connection with driving of motor vehicles) shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine of five thousand rupees (Rs. 5,000), or with both.

section: Section 182: Offences relating to licences
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 182: Offences relating to licences
Whoever drives a motor vehicle while disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence, or obtains or applies for a licence while disqualified, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine of ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000), or with both.

Section 182A: Punishment for offences relating to construction, maintenance, and sale of motor vehicles
Any person who alters a motor vehicle, including parts or components, in contravention of Chapter VII, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine of one lakh rupees (Rs. 1,00,000) per vehicle.

verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 184: Driving dangerously (Dangerous Driving / Rash Driving / Red Light Jumping / Handheld Mobile Use while driving)
Whoever drives a motor vehicle at a speed or in a manner which is dangerous to the public, having regard to all the circumstances of the case, including jumping a red light, violating stop signs, using handheld communications devices (mobile phones) while driving, or passing or overtaking other vehicles in a manner contrary to law, shall be punishable:
(a) For the first offence, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which shall not be less than one thousand rupees (Rs. 1,000) but may extend to five thousand rupees (Rs. 5,000), or with both;
(b) For any second or subsequent offence committed within three years of the previous offence, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine of ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000), or with both.

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)
section: Section 185: Driving by a drunken person or by a person under the influence of drugs (Drunk Driving)
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 185: Driving by a drunken person or by a person under the influence of drugs (Drunk Driving)
Whoever, while driving or attempting to drive a motor vehicle:
(a) Has in his blood, alcohol exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml of blood detected in a test by a breath analyser; or
(b) Is under the influence of a drug to such an extent as to be incapable of exercising proper control over the vehicle,
shall be punishable:
(i) For the first offence, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine of ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000), or with both;
(ii) For any second or subsequent offence committed within three years, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine of fifteen thousand rupees (Rs. 15,000), or with both.

section: Section 186: Driving when mentally or physically unfit to drive
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 186: Driving when mentally or physically unfit to drive
Whoever drives a motor vehicle in any public place when he is to his knowledge suffering from any disease or disability calculated to cause his driving of the vehicle to be a source of danger to the public, shall be punishable:
(a) For the first offence, with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees (Rs. 1,000);
(b) For any second or subsequent offence, with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees (Rs. 2,000).

verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 189: Racing and trials of speed
Whoever without the written consent of the State Government permits or takes part in a race or trial of speed between motor vehicles in any public place shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine of five thousand rupees (Rs. 5,000), or with both. For a second or subsequent offence, imprisonment up to one year, or fine of ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000), or both.

Section 190: Using vehicle in unsafe condition
(1) Any person who drives or causes or allows to be driven in any public place a motor vehicle or trailer, which has any defect which causes or is likely to cause danger to the public, shall be punishable with fine of one thousand five hundred rupees (Rs. 1,500).
(2) Violation of standards relating to road safety, noise, or air pollution (No PUC certificate): punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine of up to ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000), or with both, and licence disqualification for three months.

Section 192: Using vehicle without registration (Unregistered Vehicle)
Whoever drives or causes or allows to be driven a motor vehicle without registration shall be punishable:
(a) For the first offence, with a fine which shall not be less than two thousand rupees (Rs. 2,000) but may extend to five thousand rupees (Rs. 5,000);
(b) For any second or subsequent offence, with imprisonment which may extend to one year, or with fine which shall not be less than five thousand rupees (Rs. 5,000) but may extend to ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000), or with both.

Section 192A: Using vehicle without permit (Commercial vehicles)
Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be used in contravention of the provisions of sub-section (1) of Section 66 or in contravention of any condition of a permit shall be punishable:
For the first offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, and with fine of ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000);
For a subsequent offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, and with fine of ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000).

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)
section: Section 194: Driving vehicle exceeding permissible weight (Overloading of Goods Vehicles)
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 194: Driving vehicle exceeding permissible weight (Overloading of Goods Vehicles)
Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be driven in contravention of the provisions of Section 113 or Section 114 or Section 115 (overloading) shall be punishable:
With a minimum fine of twenty thousand rupees (Rs. 20,000), and an additional fine of two thousand rupees (Rs. 2,000) per tonne of excess load, together with the liability to pay charges for off-loading the excess weight.

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)
section: Section 194A: Carriage of excess passengers (Overloading in Passenger Vehicles)
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 194A: Carriage of excess passengers (Overloading in Passenger Vehicles)
Whoever drives a transport vehicle or causes or allows a transport vehicle to be driven while carrying more passengers than is permissible shall be punishable:
With a fine of two hundred rupees (Rs. 200) for each excess passenger.

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)
section: Section 194B: Use of safety belts and seating of children (Seatbelt Violation)
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 194B: Use of safety belts and seating of children (Seatbelt Violation)
(1) Whoever drives a motor vehicle without wearing a safety belt or carries passengers not wearing seat belts shall be punishable with a fine of one thousand rupees (Rs. 1,000).
(2) Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be driven with a child who, not having attained the age of fourteen years, is not secured by a safety belt or child restraint system, shall be punishable with a fine of one thousand rupees (Rs. 1,000).

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)
section: Section 194C: Penalty for violation of safety measures for motorcycle drivers and pillion riders (Helmet Violation and Triple Riding)
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 194C: Penalty for violation of safety measures for motorcycle drivers and pillion riders (Helmet Violation and Triple Riding)
Whoever drives a motorcycle or causes or allows a motorcycle to be driven in contravention of the provisions of Section 128 (carrying more than one person in addition to the driver / triple riding) or Section 129 (riding without protective headgear conforming to standards / without helmet) shall be punishable:
With a fine of one thousand rupees (Rs. 1,000) and the driver shall be disqualified for holding a driving licence for a period of three months.

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)
section: Section 194D: Penalty for not wearing protective headgear (No Helmet)
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 194D: Penalty for not wearing protective headgear (No Helmet)
Whoever drives a motorcycle or causes or allows a motorcycle to be driven without wearing protective headgear (helmet) conforming to the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) shall be punishable with a fine of one thousand rupees (Rs. 1,000) and disqualification of the driving licence for three months.

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)
section: Section 194E: Failure to allow free passage to emergency vehicles (Ambulance, Fire Brigade)
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 194E: Failure to allow free passage to emergency vehicles (Ambulance, Fire Brigade)
Whoever while driving a motor vehicle fails to draw to the side of the roadway, on the approach of a fire service vehicle or of an ambulance or other emergency vehicle as designated, shall be punishable:
With imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with a fine of ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000), or with both.

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)
section: Section 194F: Use of horns and silence zones
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 194F: Use of horns and silence zones
Whoever uses any vehicle horn needlessly or continuously or in a silence zone, or drives a vehicle which is fitted with any multi-toned horn or unauthorized siren, shall be punishable:
(a) For the first offence, with a fine of one thousand rupees (Rs. 1,000);
(b) For any second or subsequent offence, with a fine of two thousand rupees (Rs. 2,000).

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)
section: Section 196: Driving uninsured vehicle (No Motor Insurance)
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 196: Driving uninsured vehicle (No Motor Insurance)
Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be driven in contravention of the provisions of Section 146 (necessity for insurance against third party risk) shall be punishable:
(a) For the first offence, with imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine of two thousand rupees (Rs. 2,000), or with both;
(b) For any subsequent offence, with imprisonment which may extend to three months, or with fine of four thousand rupees (Rs. 4,000), or with both.

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)
section: Section 199A: Offences by juveniles (Underage Driving by Minor)
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 199A: Offences by juveniles (Underage Driving by Minor)
(1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a juvenile, the guardian of such juvenile or the owner of the motor vehicle shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished:
Punishment: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with fine of twenty-five thousand rupees (Rs. 25,000).
Registration cancellation: The registration of the motor vehicle used in the offence shall be cancelled for a period of twelve months.
Juvenile eligibility: The juvenile shall not be eligible to be granted a driving licence under Section 9 or learner's licence under Section 8 until such juvenile has attained the age of twenty-five years.

officialTitle: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act No. 32 of 2019)
section: Section 200: Composition of certain offences (Compounding of fines)
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 200: Composition of certain offences (Compounding of fines)
Any offence punishable under Section 177, 178, 179, 180, 181, 182, 183, 184, 186, 189, 190, 192, 194, 194A, 194B, 194C, 194D, 194E, 194F, 196 may, either before or after the institution of the prosecution, be compounded by such officers or authorities and for such amount as the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify in this behalf.

text: In exercise of the powers conferred by section 118 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (59 of 1988), the Central Government hereby makes the Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017 to specify the statutory rules of the road and driver conduct throughout India:

officialTitle: Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017 (Rules of the Road)
section: General Statutory Provision

text:
Regulation 5 & 6: Lane Driving, Lane Changing and Keeping to the Left
(1) Every driver of a motor vehicle shall drive the vehicle as close to the left side of the road as is practicable, allowing oncoming traffic to pass on the right.
(2) On multi-lane roads, drivers shall adhere strictly to their designated lane. Lane changing without prior indicator signalling at least three seconds before the manoeuvre is an offence under Section 177A.
(3) The extreme right lane on divided carriageways is reserved exclusively for overtaking and emergency vehicles.

officialTitle: Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017 (Rules of the Road)
section: General Statutory Provision
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Regulation 11: Duty towards Pedestrians at Zebra Crossings
(1) Pedestrians have absolute right of way at all uncontrolled pedestrian crossings (zebra crossings).
(2) Every driver approaching an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing shall slow down and come to a complete stop before the stop line to allow pedestrians to cross.
(3) Stopping or parking a motor vehicle on or within five metres of a pedestrian crossing is strictly prohibited. Violation is punishable under Section 177 and Section 184.

officialTitle: Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017 (Rules of the Road)
section: General Statutory Provision
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Regulation 14: Overtaking Regulations
(1) The driver of a motor vehicle shall overtake other vehicles only on the right side.
(2) Overtaking on the left is permitted only when the vehicle being overtaken is signalling to turn right.
(3) Overtaking is strictly prohibited:
(a) At pedestrian crossings, intersections, and railway level crossings;
(b) On blind bends, hill crests, or narrow bridges;
(c) Where the road is marked with a solid continuous white or yellow line.

officialTitle: Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017 (Rules of the Road)
section: General Statutory Provision
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Regulation 16: Roundabout Navigation and Right of Way
(1) When entering a roundabout, drivers shall yield right of way to vehicles already circulating on the roundabout from their right.
(2) Drivers shall signal their intention before entering and exiting the roundabout.

text:
Regulation 27: Duty to Give Free Passage to Emergency Vehicles
(1) On the approach of an emergency vehicle (fire service tender, ambulance, or police escort) sounding an auditory siren or displaying flashing emergency beacons, every driver shall immediately draw their vehicle to the extreme left and stop.
(2) Tailing or closely following an emergency vehicle within fifty metres is prohibited. Failure to yield free passage is an offence under Section 194E with mandatory fine of ten thousand rupees (Rs. 10,000).

officialTitle: Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017 (Rules of the Road)
section: General Statutory Provision
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Regulation 30: Use of Vehicle Horns and Silence Zones
(1) Drivers shall sound the horn only when necessary for safety to warn other road users of imminent danger.
(2) Sounding horn in designated silence zones (hospitals, schools, courts) or fitting multi-toned or pressure horns is strictly prohibited under Section 194F.

officialTitle: National Highways Act 1956 Regulations
section: Section 4: National highways to vest in the Union
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 4: National highways to vest in the Union
All national highways shall vest in the Union, and for the purposes of this Act "highways" include all lands appurtenant thereto, whether demarcated or not; all bridges, culverts, tunnels, causeways, carriageways and other structures constructed on or across such highways.

officialTitle: National Highways Act 1956 Regulations
section: Section 8A: Power of Central Government to enter into agreements for development and maintenance
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 8A: Power of Central Government to enter into agreements for development and maintenance
The Central Government may enter into an agreement with any person in relation to the development and maintenance of the whole or any part of a national highway, including collection of fee for services or benefits rendered on such highway (FASTag and electronic toll collection).

officialTitle: National Highways Act 1956 Regulations
section: Section 24 of Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002: Prevention of unauthorized highway access and encroachment
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 24 of Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002: Prevention of unauthorized highway access and encroachment
No person shall occupy any highway land or discharge any trade effluent or obstruct highway traffic without permission. Unauthorized structures or barricades on National Highways are subject to immediate demolition and statutory removal with costs assessed against the encroacher.

officialTitle: Road Transport Corporations Act 1950
section: Section 3: Establishment of Road Transport Corporations in the States
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Section 3: Establishment of Road Transport Corporations in the States
The State Government, having regard to the advantages to the public, trade and industry, and the desirability of coordinating road transport with other forms of transport, may, by notification in the Official Gazette, establish a Road Transport Corporation for the whole or any part of the State.

verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority

Section 34: Directions by the State Government
The State Government may, after consultation with the Corporation, give to the Corporation general instructions to be followed by the Corporation, and such instructions may include directions relating to the recruitment, conditions of service and training of its employees, wages, and passenger safety fares.

State Statutory Rules governing omnibus operations, stage carriages, driver safety certifications, and road safety councils across Tamil Nadu

officialTitle: Tamil Nadu Motor Vehicles Rules 1989
section: Rule 15: Special Conditions for State Passenger Stage Carriages
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 15: Special Conditions for State Passenger Stage Carriages
Every stage carriage operating in Tamil Nadu shall provide reserved seating for women, senior citizens, and persons with disabilities. Automatic pneumatic passenger doors or safety bar gates shall be maintained in working condition while the vehicle is in motion to prevent falls from footboards.

officialTitle: Tamil Nadu Motor Vehicles Rules 1989
section: Rule 278: Tamil Nadu State Road Safety Council and District Road Safety Committees
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 278: Tamil Nadu State Road Safety Council and District Road Safety Committees
The State Government constitutes the Tamil Nadu State Road Safety Council headed by the Minister for Transport, along with District Road Safety Committees chaired by District Collectors, to review accident fatality reduction targets, identify black spots on State Highways, and monitor road safety funds.

officialTitle: Tamil Nadu Motor Vehicles Rules 1989
section: Rule 348: Prohibition of Audio and Visual Distractions in Transport Vehicles
verifiedBy: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) Gazette Authority
text:
Rule 348: Prohibition of Audio and Visual Distractions in Transport Vehicles
Fitting of video playback screens or loudspeakers within the sight or immediate hearing range of the driver while operating transport buses or omnibuses is prohibited to prevent distraction. Violation constitutes an offence under Section 177 of the Act.
